statements.status_notes: CVE-2011-3389 (BEAST) is a weakness of the CBC cipher suites in SSL 3.0 and TLS 1.0, whose chained initialization vectors let a man-in-the-middle who can inject chosen plaintext into a connection recover parts of it; TLS 1.1 and later use explicit IVs. Debian lists gnutls28 in trixie as unfixed (unimportant) and notes that GnuTLS has no mitigation other than using TLS 1.1 or later: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2011-3389. GnuTLS 3.8.14 added a --enable-tls11-support configure option, following RFC 8996, that builds the library without TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 and DTLS 1.0 (https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/4ff381e68dbe9173ade2c4d8fe7f0b0ce0077edb); upstream leaves it enabled by default. The DHI gnutls28 build at the fixed version below carries that option and is configured with it disabled. Checked in the published libgnutls30t64 packages of that build for amd64 and arm64: the library's protocol table marks SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1, DTLS 0.9 and DTLS 1.0 as unsupported, obsolete and not revertible, and its built-in protocol priority lists hold only TLS 1.3, TLS 1.2 and DTLS 1.2, so an application using this library cannot negotiate a protocol version BEAST applies to; the gnutls-cli-debug program in gnutls-bin no longer carries its TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 probes. The build published before it, made from the same Debian 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 source, still marks TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 and DTLS 1.0 as supported and is reported as affected, as are builds of Debian's earlier 3.8.9-3+deb13u2 and 3.8.9-3+deb13u3 sources, which sort below the boundary. Recorded as FIXED rather than not affected because the protection ships in a specific build of this package and earlier builds can still negotiate TLS 1.0.
